questions.question: What is the specificity difference between a type, class, and id selector?
questions.answer: Specificity is (ids, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, elements/pseudo-elements). Type = 0,0,1; class = 0,1,0; id = 1,0,0; universal = 0,0,0.

questions.question: List the four combinators and what each matches.
questions.answer: Descendant (space) matches any descendant; child (>) matches direct children; adjacent sibling (+) matches the next sibling; general sibling (~) matches all later siblings under the same parent.

questions.question: What do :is(), :where(), and :not() do?
questions.answer: :is() matches any selector in a list at the highest specificity among them. :where() matches similarly but contributes zero specificity. :not() excludes elements matching its argument.

questions.question: Why should pseudo-elements not carry essential content?
questions.answer: ::before/::after generate boxes that are not in the DOM; some screen readers ignore them, they cannot be selected/copied reliably, and they need a content value. Use real markup for meaningful text.

questions.question: Style external links and PDF links differently for Kakade's docs.
Give cards a 3px accent bar and zero-margin headings using low-specificity selectors.
Why is #hero .title harder to override than .hero .title?
questions.answer: The id adds a full id-specificity point (1,0,0 plus class), so only another id selector, an inline style, or !important can beat it. Classes keep specificity low and overridable.

questions.question: What is the difference between :nth-child(2) and :nth-of-type(2)?
questions.answer: :nth-child(2) matches an element that is the second child of its parent regardless of type. :nth-of-type(2) matches the second sibling of that specific element type.
